0.0.n: 周り refers here to the people surrounding her, rather than her physical surroundings.

0.1.n: の links the people around her to their opposition.

0.2.n: 反対 means disapproval of the path she wanted to take.

0.3.n: も presents the opposition as an additional factor in her decision.

0.4.n: あり is a linking form of ある, connecting the existence of opposition to what follows.

0.6.n: 一度 describes an earlier choice that she later reconsidered.

0.7.n: は highlights 一度, contrasting her initial choice with her later change of direction.

0.8.n: 他 combines with の and a noun to describe something different.

0.9.n: の connects 他 to 道; together, 他の道 means another path.

0.10.n: 道 is figurative here, referring to a direction in life or work.

0.11.n: に marks the direction she takes with 進む.

0.12.n: 進みます is the polite form of 進む; this narrative uses present forms to recount past events.

0.13.n: が connects this choice to a contrasting development in the next line.

1.0.n: 諦める combines with きる for completeness; きれず means being unable to do it fully and links to what follows.

1.2.n: 歳 follows a number to express someone's age.

1.3.n: の links her age to 時, forming an expression meaning when she was that age.

1.4.n: 時 follows the age expression to identify when she took action.

1.6.n: 門をたたく literally describes knocking at a gate, but here means approaching a master to seek instruction.

1.7.n: を marks 門 as the thing being knocked on.

1.8.n: たたきます is the polite form of たたく, used here within an expression about seeking instruction.

2.0.n: その points back to the time when she approached the master.

2.1.n: その時 sets the time for the description that follows.

2.3.n: 歳 marks age; this age describes her son, not her.

2.4.n: の connects the age expression to 息子, describing how old he is.

2.5.n: 息子 refers here to her male child.

2.6.n: が marks 息子 as the person whose existence is expressed by いる.

2.7.n: いる expresses existence for living things; 息子がいる describes the mother as having a son.

2.8.n: シングルマザー is an English loanword written in katakana.

2.9.n: でし is the part of でした before た; the complete ending politely states a past situation.

2.10.n: た completes でした, placing her situation at that earlier time.

0.lit: There also being opposition from those around her, once she proceeds onto another path, but…
0.tip: The final が signals a contrast that continues into the next line.

1.lit: Unable to give up completely, at the time of age 27, she knocks at the gate.
1.tip: 門をたたく is an expression for approaching a teacher or master to seek instruction.

2.lit: At that time, she was a single mother who has a three-year-old son.
2.tip: ３歳の息子がいる comes before シングルマザー and describes her as having a three-year-old son.
